questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The language and course options.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Everything has been easy to find.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had 2 orientation days with information and we were made aware of the International Office.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy because the host university had an online formula to fill out and quickly after that I received an offer for accomodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I don't know. I did not live far from the campus, so that was fortunate.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to find the courses I wanted, check the timetable and make sure that I would not have any overlapping lectures. When I had found the courses that made sense for my interests and the timetable, I had to choose them on an online site provided by the university. It was very easy to figure out and we were informed how to do it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We were sent a document with the whole process step by step and we were informed on the process at orientation day.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successfull, everything happened as I expected.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just read though the document they will sent you and it will be easy to figure out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had 5 courses out of which 4 was absolutely amazing and 1 which I did not like based on the way the lecturer conducted the course.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only took courses on bachelor level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
I did not differ much in teaching style, but there was a slight difference in the structure of the course. 
Although the one course I did not enjoy was mainly because of the teaching style, where we were given minimum to no readings at all, and the lecturer had a condescending attitude towards the students - in my opinion. I do not believe this reflects the host university in general as it has been amazing overall! It was only that one lecturer.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
EN3005 Introduction to Irish Literature
FL2012 Exploring the Otherworld: Popular Belief and Symbols
FL2111 Aspects of Irish Folklore 
FL3013 Studying Stories: Theory and Method
FL3015 Indigenous Knowledge: Herbs and Healing in Irish Folklore

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I will definitely recommend the first 4 mentioned as they are extremely interesting and a great way to understand Irish culture.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had not thought about money spent on doing laundry.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food is generally a bit cheaper, but not by much. 
Transport is much cheaper. 
Accomodation/housing is quite expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Multiple! I think there was a club or society for almost anything - at least there was many more options than I could imagine.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the Yoga and Meditation society where I could attend a session and relax - because it can be quite stressfull to be an exchange student.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend goind on trips around the country, fx. to see the Cliffs of Moher, Blarner Castle, Rock of Cashel, Killarney National Park etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy as it was a European country.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs and societies!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don't think I have had any cultural challenges with Ireland and Irish people - it would more so be with the other exchange student from all over the world with culture very different to mine.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The festivals, traditions and the kind mindset.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Join the clubs and societies. Enjoy the beautiful campus and lecture halls. Engage in the courses you find interesting.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I do not think I have any more advice to give.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: That I have had the chance to explore another culture and country through interesting courses which has broadened my horizon and impacted me both acedemicly and personally.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge for me was to figure out the academic expectations and how to live up to it. Not that they expected much, but just how to go about the study system in another country.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
